q-80656.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14180816/assets/5c6e4deccce395f5bdc8aadef8cd2c712804235c340ccae174f2067211a5a49c.png)

Consider the region $R$ shown above. Let the function $f(x,y)$ be defined as

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}{e}^{x}, & (x,y)\in S, \\ {x}^{2}+y, & (x,y)\in T, \\ 0, & (x,y)\in U.\end{aligned}
$$

Then,

$$
{∬}_{R}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A=
$$
q-80656.worked_solution:
First, notice that the domain $R$ can be represented as a union of three sub-domains, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}R & =S\cup T\cup U.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{S}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{T}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{U}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{S}{e}^{x}\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{T}({x}^{2}+y)\text{d}A+{∬}_{U}0\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{S}{e}^{x}\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{T}({x}^{2}+y)\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

q-81244.name: Question 3
q-81244.worked_solution:
Using the linearity property of double integrals, we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}({x}^{2}-y+1)\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{R}{x}^{2}\text{ }\text{d}A-{∬}_{R}y\text{ }\text{d}A+{∬}_{R}\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

The function under the first integral is independent of $y.$ So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}{x}^{2}\text{ }\text{d}A & =(4-0){\int }_{-3}^{0}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =4[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}]_{-3}^{0} \\  & =4(\frac{{0}^{3}}{3}-\frac{(-3)^{3}}{3}) \\  & =36.\end{aligned}
$$

The function under the second integral is independent of $x.$ So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}y\text{ }\text{d}A & =(0-(-3)){\int }_{0}^{4}y\,\text{d}y \\  & =3[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]_{0}^{4} \\  & =3(\frac{{4}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{0}^{2}}{2}) \\  & =24.\end{aligned}
$$

The third integral is the double integral of unity:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}\text{d}A=\text{Area}(R)=3\cdot 4=12\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, combining our results, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}({x}^{2}-y+1)\,\text{d}A=36-24+12=24.\end{aligned}
$$

?

a
0
b
12

24

36

Using the linearity property of double integrals, we can write

∬R(x2−y+1)dA=∬Rx2 dA−∬Ry dA+∬RdA.

The function under the first integral is independent of y. So, we have

∬Rx2 dA=(4−0)∫−30x2dx=4[x33]−30=4(033−(−3)33)=36.

The function under the second integral is independent of x. So, we have

∬Ry dA=(0−(−3))∫04ydy=3[y22]04=3(422−022)=24.

The third integral is the double integral of unity:

∬RdA=Area(R)=3⋅4=12

Finally, combining our results, we obtain

∬R(x2−y+1)dA=36−24+12=24.

q-81253.name: Question 4
q-81253.problem:
Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A$, where

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡y,\, & \text{if}\,-1<x<1,\,0<y<\pi , \\ x\operatorname{sin}⁡y,\, & \text{if}\,1<x<2,\,0<y<\pi ,\end{aligned}
$$

and  $R$ is the domain of $f.$
q-81253.worked_solution:
First, notice that we have $R={R}_{1}\cup {R}_{2}$, where ${R}_{1}=(-1,1)\times (0,\pi )$ and ${R}_{2}=(1,2)\times (0,\pi ).$ So, we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A= & ={∬}_{{R}_{1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{{R}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{{R}_{1}}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{{R}_{2}}x\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,\text{d}A \\  & =(1-(-1)){\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,\text{d}y+({\int }_{1}^{2}x\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,\text{d}y) \\  & =2[\operatorname{sin}⁡y]_{0}^{\pi }+[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]_{1}^{2}\cdot [-\operatorname{cos}⁡y]_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =2(0)+(2-\frac{1}{2})\cdot (-(-1)+1) \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

q-130021.worked_solution:
Using the linearity and additivity of double integrals, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{C\cup D}5f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A & =\frac{1}{3}{∬}_{C\cup D}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{1}{3}({∬}_{C}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A+{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(7+2) \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$
